_note: Short, original descriptions written for this project's embedding corpus -- not verbatim MITRE text. technique_id/technique_name/tactic are the official public ATT&CK identifiers. Extend this list with more techniques as needed; each entry's 'description' is what gets embedded, so keep it behaviorally specific, not just a restatement of the name.

techniques.description: Adversary or script invokes PowerShell to execute commands, download payloads, or run encoded scripts, often spawned from another process rather than typed interactively.
A user opens or double-clicks a file (often disguised with a misleading icon or extension) that launches a malicious executable or script, typically with explorer.exe as the parent process.
A file name contains a Unicode right-to-left override control character to visually reverse part of the filename, disguising a dangerous extension as something benign.
A process opens a handle to lsass.exe with memory-read access rights in order to extract credentials, password hashes, or Kerberos tickets from process memory.
A process allocates memory in or injects code into another running process to execute in that process's context, evading process-based defenses.
Network communication uses DNS queries and responses to exfiltrate data or receive commands, blending in with normal name-resolution traffic.
An actor uses valid credentials to connect to another host over RDP, enabling interactive lateral movement across the network.
A scheduled task is created or modified to execute a program at a specified time or system event, providing a persistence mechanism.

techniques.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
techniques.description: A registry run key or startup folder entry is created so a program executes automatically when a user logs on, establishing persistence.

techniques.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Security software, logging, or monitoring tools are disabled, uninstalled, or reconfigured to reduce visibility into subsequent malicious activity.
An actor enumerates other systems on the network, such as via ping sweeps, ARP cache inspection, or directory service queries, to map the environment.
Commands are run to gather details about the operating system, hardware, patch level, or configuration of the local host.
Files on a system or across a network are encrypted, typically as part of a ransomware operation intended to disrupt availability.
Data is transferred out of the network using a protocol different from the primary command-and-control channel, such as FTP or an unencrypted web upload.
A targeted email contains a malicious file attachment that, once opened by the victim, executes attacker code on the host.
